title: CIMD Lab: client ID metadata documents, both directions

glossary.definition: Client ID Metadata Document. The client's client_id is an https URL, and the authorization server fetches the JSON document behind it instead of requiring registration first.
An https URL with a path, no fragment, no query and no credentials. The document served there must repeat the same URL as its client_id.
The older way to avoid manual registration: the client POSTs its metadata and the server keeps a record. CIMD keeps no record per client up front.
A stranger chooses the document URL, so the server refuses private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses, redirects, oversize bodies and slow answers.
PingFederate is the authorization server and the lab is the client. Real PingFederate only; there is no mock of it.
The lab's own teaching authorization server accepts a URL as client_id, and a tester shows each way a document is refused.

Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant (slide 36 of Ping's H2 2026 deck): the MCP specification now prefers CIMD over dynamic registration, a client identifies itself by a document URL the tenant has allowlisted, and the gateway fetches, validates and caches it and advertises support in its discovery metadata; its authorization server also offers dynamic client registration. The lab's tab is a local simulation, not PingFederate and not the gateway.

Every row of the H2 2026 tab carries one tag: deck claim, console swagger name (schema only), lab reading, lab-invented, or measured (our note). A swagger name proves a field exists, not how it behaves; a lab reading or lab-invented rule is not something the deck says.

cards.label: Why it matters: the MCP gateway (Ping's words)
cards.description: Ping claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Challenge: one shared token and every tool exposed to every caller, so security stalls adoption. Technical: per-user identity, per-tool policy and injected credentials on every call, fully audited. Business: MCP integrations proceed under existing governance; faster time to value on agent projects.
